key_points: Abnormal uterine bleeding is categorized as dysfunctional (physiologic) or organic (polyps, cancer, infection).
The menstrual cycle has proliferative (follicular) and secretory (luteal) phases; progesterone withdrawal triggers menstruation.
Low-dose birth control pills (15-25 mcg estrogen) must be started in the first three days of the cycle to prevent ovulation.
Perimenopause onset is defined by irregular periods (interval, flow, or duration), not hot flashes; average onset age is 45.
Menopause is diagnosed after 12 months of amenorrhea; average age is 52, with 90% of women menopausal by age 54.
In perimenopause, low-dose estrogen OCPs can regulate cycles; consider progesterone-only pills if DVT history.
Hypothalamic amenorrhea from stress (e.g., death, divorce, illness) is common; ask about life stressors before extensive labs.
Chronic anovulation has two main causes: PCOS and insulin resistance; check A1c and evaluate for PCOS.
PCOS diagnosis requires two of three: irregular periods, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, elevated testosterone (or clinical hirsutism).
In young girls with irregular periods, observe for up to two years before intervening, as physiology takes time to stabilize.
